name: Merelani Hills
desc: The only known source of Tanzanite on Earth. The gem was discovered here in 1967, in the foothills of Mount Kilimanjaro.

name: Lemshuku & Komolo
desc: Source of tsavorite, the vivid green grossular garnet first identified in this part of northern Tanzania in the late 1960s.

name: Landanai
desc: Known for deep green chrome tourmaline, coloured by traces of chromium and vanadium.

name: Lake Manyara
desc: Mines near the shores of Lake Manyara produce emerald and the colour-change gem alexandrite.

name: Longido
desc: Famous for anyolite — red ruby crystals set in green zoisite, a striking material used for carvings and cabochons.

name: Winza
desc: A ruby deposit that drew worldwide attention after its discovery in 2007, producing rich red stones.

name: Haneti
desc: A source of apple-green chrysoprase, polished into cabochons, beads and carvings.

name: Matombo & Uluguru Mountains
desc: The hills south of Morogoro have long produced ruby, sapphire and rhodolite garnet.

name: Mahenge
desc: World-renowned for vivid pink and red spinel. The area also yields ruby and garnet, and hosts large graphite deposits.

name: Umba Valley
desc: Known for sapphires in many colours and for Malaya garnet, first found here. Rhodolite and tourmaline also occur.

name: Tunduru
desc: One of Africa's richest gem gravels, yielding an extraordinary variety of sapphire, spinel, alexandrite and more.

name: Songea
desc: Alluvial deposits around Songea produce sapphires in a wide range of colours, along with garnet and zircon.

name: Mwadui (Williamson Mine)
desc: The Williamson diamond mine, one of Africa's historic diamond mines, in production since the 1940s.

name: Geita
desc: The heart of the Lake Victoria goldfields and home to one of Tanzania's largest gold mines.

name: Bulyanhulu
desc: An underground mine producing gold together with copper and silver.

name: North Mara
desc: A major gold-mining area in the Mara Region, east of Lake Victoria.

name: Lupa Goldfield
desc: A historic goldfield in the southern highlands, worked since the 1920s.

name: Mpanda
desc: A mineralised belt in western Tanzania with gold and copper occurrences.

name: Kabanga
desc: One of the world's significant nickel sulphide deposits, near the Burundi border.

name: Ngualla
desc: A rare-earth deposit in the southern highlands, important for magnets used in modern technology.

name: Panda Hill
desc: A carbonatite deposit near Mbeya containing niobium, used in high-strength steel.

name: Ruangwa & Nachingwea
desc: Part of south-east Tanzania's graphite belt, a key material for batteries.

name: Mchuchuma & Liganga
desc: Large coal and iron-ore deposits in the southern highlands near Lake Nyasa.

name: Lake Natron
desc: An alkaline lake rich in soda ash, and a famous breeding ground for lesser flamingos.

name: Songo Songo
desc: An offshore island gas field supplying much of Dar es Salaam's power generation.

name: Mnazi Bay
desc: A coastal gas field near Mtwara in the far south-east.
